subject: Vanguard-X3B incident: elevated 5xx/timeouts — mitigations and closure
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanguard Ops <ops@vanguard-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vanguard-X3B — elevated 5xx/timeouts (mitigations & timeline)

Hi Tara / Vanguard team,

We observed a spike in 5xx errors and timeouts against your Vanguard-X3B model beginning ~08:58 PDT this morning (first detections at 09:02 PDT). Symptoms: 10–30% of requests returned 5xx or timed out, with a corresponding client-visible latency increase for streaming responses.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled traffic away from the recent quantized kernel rollout (v1.4) to the previous stable kernel across the affected fleet.
- Shifted a portion of Vanguard requests to the X2B variant (automated fallback) to keep throughput stable while we triage.
- Temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity for your reserved nodes and bumped autoscaler to faster policy to reduce queueing.
- Enabled prefix/KV cache retention for hot keys and increased retry/backoff guidance in the SDK (recommended client-side 500+ms exponential backoff).

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (initial timestamps), initial-snapshot.json (edge metrics snapshot).

Immediate ask: Please keep retries enabled on your side and avoid large fanouts for the next 2 hours while we verify stabilization. We’ll provide an interim update within 2–3 hours and a follow-up postmortem.

Short-term expected impact: degraded success rate for a subset of calls until the kernel revert stabilizes caches; no customer data was exposed.

I’ll keep you posted; tagging Ben and Karthik for infra/serving follow-up.

—
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Tara Singh <tara@vanguard-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vanguard-X3B — elevated 5xx/timeouts (mitigations & timeline)

Thanks Monica. Our ingestion pipeline saw retries spike and a few client-side failures; we toggled retries immediately. Two quick questions:

1) Do you have an estimate for MTTR and whether this qualifies under the uptime SLA for Vanguard (we'll need to assess potential credits)?
2) Can you confirm whether you captured full request/response logs for the affected window and whether we can share them with our SREs for correlation?

We appreciate the rapid response — please keep us posted on root cause.

—
Tara Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, Vanguard Analytics
ops@vanguard-analytics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Vanguard-X3B — elevated 5xx/timeouts (mitigations & timeline)

Monica — quick internal notes / recommendation: 
- We should fully revert the quantized-kernel v1.4 on the Vanguard fleet and pin to v1.3 for 24–48 hrs. The canary showed increased cache churn in memory profiles.
- Opened RAW-8492 to track kernel revert + CI regression test. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RAW-8492
- Plan: revert at 10:30 PDT, run a graduated canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with KV cache monitoring (metrics: kv_eviction_rate, kv_hit_ratio, workqueue-latency). If we see mem growth > 15% over baseline, halt.
- Ops: schedule a short maintenance window for the revert and notify affected customers. The fallback to X2B is holding, but we should avoid prolonged fallback if the revert is quick.

Karthik — can you prepare the kernel revert runbook and confirm rollback steps? I’ll coordinate capacity for the short autoscale bump.

—Ben

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanguard Ops <ops@vanguard-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-24T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Vanguard-X3B — service restored (interim findings & next steps)

Tara / team,

Update: Service restored to normal success rates around 12:50 PDT after we reverted the quantized kernel v1.4 to v1.3 and completed the canary rollout. Current status: 99.95% success rate across Vanguard routes and normal latency distributions.

Interim findings:
- Root trigger: a change in the quantized kernel's KV cache eviction policy introduced higher-than-expected churn under the Vanguard request profile. This caused increased memory pressure on inference workers, which in turn led to OOM-driven request aborts and throttling that surfaced as 5xx/timeouts.
- Impact window: ~08:58–12:50 PDT.

What we've done:
- Reverted kernel to v1.3; patched autoscaler to be more aggressive temporary scaling for fleets with high kv_eviction_rate.
- Added an alert on kv_eviction_rate > 0.1 and sustained mem growth over 10% in 5m windows.
- Created RAW-8492 for full RCA and follow-up remediation work.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx (draft RCA + timeline).

Next steps:
- We will produce a finalized postmortem by EOD Friday (2026-06-26).
- Offer a technical review session (30–45 min) next week to walk the RCA and permanent mitigations. Are you available Tues/Wed?
- We will provide the full request/response logs for the affected window (safely redacted) and the incident timeline CSV.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience. If you need immediate assistance with retries/backoff or want us to enable an extra dedicated burst for your account while we complete the RCA, let me know and we can arrange it.

—
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Vanguard Analytics <ops@vanguard-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Vanguard-X3B — final postmortem and remediation checklist

Hi Tara — final postmortem attached and summary below. Thanks again for your patience while we completed the investigation.

Final summary (attached final-postmortem.pdf):
- Root cause: regression in quantized kernel v1.4 that altered KV cache eviction heuristics. Under Vanguard's request distribution (high prefix locality with many short-lived keys), this caused rapid eviction and cache thrash, resulting in memory pressure and worker-level OOMs; those OOMs surfaced as aborted requests and 5xx/timeouts.
- Contributing factors: insufficient canary workload coverage for prefix-locality patterns; autoscaler policy was too conservative for abrupt cache-pressure events.
- Customer impact window: 2026-06-24T08:58:00-07:00 through 2026-06-24T12:50:00-07:00.

Longer-term remediation completed/planned:
1) Kernel patch: fix KV eviction heuristic (deployed 2026-06-25, verified in staging).
2) Autoscaler change: new policy for fast-scale on kv_eviction_rate alerts (+30% faster scale-up).
3) Canary coverage: add synthetic load tests that emulate high prefix churn and short-lived keys.
4) Observability: new dashboard panels for kv_hit_ratio, kv_eviction_rate, and worker-oom-rate; alerts added for sustained mem growth.
5) Customer-side guidance: SDK backoff recommendations and optional client-side rate limiting if you run high-fanout patterns.

We’ve attached the remediation checklist and the final PDF postmortem. Please review and let us know a convenient time for a 45-min technical review next week; Karthik and Ben will join to walk through the fixes.

Regarding SLA credits: our customer success team will open a formal SLA review ticket and follow our standard adjustments process. I’ll cc them once we confirm a time to sync.

Attachments: final-postmortem.pdf, remediation-checklist.md

If you want an interim mitigation (we can temporarily keep a slightly more conservative kernel and a transient capacity credit while you complete any internal validation), we can schedule that for the next 7 days.

Thanks — we aim to prevent this recurrence.

—
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
